title: Abort active parser without updating readiness in document.open()
body:
Abort `document`'s existing active parser in the `document open steps` (after erasing event listeners and handlers, and before replacing all children with null), default `abort a parser`'s `updateReadiness` parameter to `false` (passing `true` when aborting a document), and link `active parser was aborted` to aborting a document.

When `document.open()` gated `stop loading` on an ongoing navigation ID, calling `document.open()` after navigation commit stopped aborting `document`'s existing active network or script-created parser, leaving its pending input stream and open elements active alongside the new script-created parser. Defaulting `updateReadiness` to `false` in `abort a parser` (and only passing `true` in `abort a document`) aborts the old parser in `document.open()` and fragment parsers without prematurely transitioning `readyState` or setting `domInteractive`/`domComplete` before `document.open()` sets readiness to `"loading"`.

Tests: https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/65542.

- [x] At least two implementers are interested (and none opposed):
   * Chromium (already implements this behavior)
   * Gecko (already aborts the active parser and discards remaining input; transitions readiness before erasing listeners)
   * WebKit (already implements this behavior)
- [x] [Tests](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt) are written and can be reviewed and commented upon at:
   * https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/65542
- [ ] [Implementation bugs](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests) are filed:
   * Chromium: already matching
   * Gecko: … (fails subtest 1: transitions readiness before erasing event listeners)
   * WebKit: already matching
- [x] Corresponding [HTML AAM](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/) & [ARIA in HTML](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/) issues & PRs: N/A
